title: Looking for best AI video platforms for creating cinematic game trailers?
author: Majestic_Ease_9382
selftext:
Hey everyone, I’m running a small indie studio that is looking to publish one of our first games. We’re working on our prologue teaser to showcase at an upcoming game show. While we will be using real gameplay and in-engine footage for the most part, I was looking for some AI video tools to add cinematic b-rolls based on our world and lore.

I've seen people mention Luma, Pika, invideo, and even Google Flow as options but I’m not sure which ones will work for me. For me, consistency in art direction, commercial usage and avoiding misleading visuals matters. I want to build off of our current assets, not promise something and deliver something else.

Has anyone used these tools for game trailers? Would love to hear what your experience was.

comments.author: BusThese7504
comments.body: For this I’d probably prioritize consistency over how impressive the first generation looks. If it can actually stick to your game’s art direction and build from your existing assets, that’s a huge win.

comments.author: broker415
comments.body: Do it in engine, trust me

comments.author: Houndzx
comments.body: For game trailers, both Luma and invideo are good options. I personally would give invideo a slight edge, as I found it holds art direction much better over longer projects. If you want something that maintains your artstyle and takes 3D engine captures as inputs, I would definitely consider it.

comments.author: Pristine_Good7326
comments.body: Try seedance. It can deliver fantastic aesthetic results with primary level of prompting. Of course it is best if you can give a proper thought on the split scenes first so you would save up credits.

replies.author: Pristine_Good7326
replies.body: I mean seedance 2.0 not the fast and lite version

comments.author: bemren
comments.body: I’m currently using [moodnode.ai](http://moodnode.ai) It brings all the AI engines together for image, video, and audio generation. The audio tools are especially useful for me because I can record my gameplay, add AI voiceovers, and use them for commentary.
